answer: Pay each answer by its Shapley-style marginal value: every epoch the network samples 40 random orderings of all answers and credits each only for what it adds beyond those ahead of it, so an echo of near-copies splits a single share. An attacker running N fakes must write N truly distinct contributions, since each extra copy's marginal value falls toward zero: effort grows linearly while payout stays flat. Weakness: across a canyon of thousands of answers, 40 sampled orderings are noisy, and honest agents who cut similar ideas from the same timber get underpaid.
